source_read: Publisher HTML (nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02565-4, corrected version), read in my own browser tab (tab-9; no other tab touched, nothing downloaded): every running-text paragraph counted by script; the Table 1 and Table 2 pages; Fig. 1 with its legend, Fig. 2a and Fig. 3; byline, consortia, contributions, acknowledgements, competing interests and references 12, 13 and 32; the Author Correction (nature.com/articles/s41591-024-03331-w). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04077437 through the API v2 and its version history (versions 0, 24, 25, 37 and 38). Supplementary Information and source data not read. Step 1 not run this round.

design.note: Confirmatory phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial at 13 sites.

key_findings.note: Fig. 1: 324 screened, 121 enrolled, 17 excluded, 104 randomized; on MDMA 1 chose to stop after session 3; on placebo 6 chose to stop (one with no outcome data, outside the mITT) and 2 stopped after adverse events; de jure 52 and 42 (legend footnote c: one placebo 18-week CAPS-5 with missing item-level data).
Fig. 3 prints after session 1: loss of diagnosis 39.6 vs 22.0 and responders 52.8 vs 42.0; NNTs in the text.
Recomputed Bang index 0.92 and 0.55; respondents 52 of 53 and 44 of 51.

key_findings.correction: Every number given is right, but the list leaves out three of the 17 rows of Table 2: dry mouth 9 (17.0%) vs 4 (7.8%), chills 8 (15.1%) vs 1 (2.0%) and restlessness 8 (15.1%) vs 2 (3.9%).

key_findings.note: The paragraph also gives cardiac TEAESIs in 4 vs 1, all palpitations.
Quotation and the three observations as printed.
Registry history: primary and secondary outcomes as reported since version 0 (30 August 2019, a year before the start); 'adapted' was added to the SDS title on 11 June 2021.
Window to the last integrative session, about 12 weeks; no serious events; no euphoria term.
Correction notice read: 7 October 2024, Nat Med 30, 3382; it adds only the 14 collaborator-group members, and its byline drops the full stop after 'G'.

reporting_issues.note: Text 94 + 9 = 103; CONSORT completers 52 and 43; registry completed 52 and 42, not completed 1 and 9.
Fig. 3 title n = 53 and n = 50; after session 3, 86.5% = 45/52 and 69.0% = 29/42. The denominators change by visit: after session 1 the bars use 53 and 50 (39.6% = 21/53, 22.0% = 11/50).

domains.note: Recomputed the female-at-birth imbalance: chi-square P = .013.
Also: the blinding survey lacks 7 placebo participants and 1 on MDMA; whether these are the 8 who stopped treatment is not stated.
As for MAPP1, high rests on the participant's report being part of the CAPS-5 measurement; here the unblinding is measured (94% and 75%), so the case is stronger.
The registered outcomes have not changed in substance since registration a year before the start.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial is right, with one point of balance: the authors' first expectancy observation (no separation after session 1) concerns the CAPS-5 means, which in Fig. 2a are only about 3 points apart after session 1 with overlapping s.e.m. bars; the card's counter-evidence (Fig. 3, 39.6% vs 22.0% losing the diagnosis after session 1) is real but categorical. Both should be stated.

missed: The ecstasy-use exclusion appears in the registry only since 28 October 2024 (version 38); during the trial the registry's eligibility listed 'abusing illegal drugs'. The card's inclusion_exclusion attributes it to the registry without that date.

Table 1 gives suicidal ideation (psychiatric history) in 44 (83.0%) and 47 (92.2%), 91 of 104, while Results › Safety, 5th paragraph gives 87 of 104 with a lifetime history; Brett & Bynum use the latter.

MAPP2 defines loss of diagnosis as a fall of 10 points or more and no longer meeting the diagnostic criteria (Methods › Outcomes, 2nd paragraph); MAPP1 defines it by the CAPS-5 diagnostic algorithm alone. The joined claims pool both as 'no longer met PTSD criteria'.

Recruitment methods are in the registry's participant flow (print and internet advertisements, referrals from treatment providers, word of mouth); the card says only that the main text does not give them.
